text:
clare (eng-platform): Quick sync: customers report mismatch between runtime token accounting and obsv-derived cost for requests that hit prefix/KV cache. Runtime reports ~0 tokens for some cache-hot paths but the obsv pipeline still spreads a full avg-token cost. Need a path to reconcile.

diego (runtime): Noted. Runtime does a short-circuit on cache hit (no decode loop), so GPU cycles are near-zero. We can emit a compact 'work_units' delta per request (integers) to indicate actual decode ops done.

nina (observability): We tried adding full runtime metadata before and index size ballooned. Two ideas: (A) add two concise fields to trace envelope (cache_hit:boolean, work_units:int) as low-card facets, or (B) keep trace index unchanged and publish a parallel compact cost stream keyed by trace_id for join-on-demand. (B) reduces trace cardinality but makes ad-hoc queries harder.

john (billing): From invoice accuracy POV we prefer per-request fidelity. But if cardinality kills query perf, that harms audits. Is there a middle ground?

tara (privacy): Any new field must avoid customer prompt payloads. If we send hashes or IDs, ensure irreversible. Also avoid model-internal identifiers that could leak config secrets.

diego (runtime): Implementation suggestion: ship a tiny base64 header X-RW-COST-V1 with a packed 24-bit payload: 1 bit cache_hit, 7 bits exec_bucket (0-127), 16 bits work_units (0-65535). No free-form strings. That keeps envelope small and opaque.

nina (observability): That header approach is promising. We can have the ingest pipeline decode the header and write two targets: (1) a compact topic obsv.cost.v1 for reconciliations and (2) populate derived low-cardinality fields (cache_hit, cost_bucket) into the trace index. That keeps trace index lean but gives us reconciliation path.

john (billing): If we have obsv.cost.v1 we can run a nightly job to reconcile usage with runtime ledger. Can we also emit a histogram summary per-customer per-day to avoid keeping per-request forever?

nina (observability): Yes. Plan: keep full obsv.cost.v1 for 7 days, aggregate histograms per-tenant/per-model and persist those for 90 days. That supports audits while bounding storage.

diego (runtime): We'll add the header in canary pools only initially. Proto sketch (packing):
```
// X-RW-COST-V1 (24 bits / 3 bytes)
// bit0: cache_hit (1=hit)
// bit1-7: exec_bucket (7 bits) -> coarse work bucket (0..127)
// bits8-23: work_units (16 bits unsigned)
// base64 encode 3 raw bytes to avoid proxy mangling
```

tara (privacy): Confirming: header will contain only numeric flags, no text or hashes. Good. Keep retention short for request-level stream. Also add policy: auto-delete raw stream for EU customers after 3 days unless flagged for audit.

clare (eng-platform): Operational concerns: edge proxies have 8KB header limits in some regions. base64 + 3 bytes is tiny but watch for future schema growth. Also we need ingress backpressure tests at peak TPS.

nina (observability): I'll spin up an ingest consumer that decodes header and writes to obsv.cost.v1. It will also emit daily histograms and a small derived field into trace index: cost_bucket = low/med/high, cache_hit=true/false.

john (billing): For backfill: if delta > 3% for last billing cycle, we want to apply an adjustment and optionally backfill. Otherwise forward-only. Hit me with numbers.

diego (runtime): Can do canary rollout: 1% -> 10% -> 100% over two weeks. Canary will tag hits with canary=true in X-RW-COST-V1 LSB for easy filtering.

metrics-bot: New topic created: kafka://obsv.cost.v1 (owned by nina). Canary consumer: obsv-cost-canary-01.

clare (eng-platform): Action list: diego -> PR adding header + serializer to runtime canary (ETA Mon), nina -> consumer + dashboard + daily histogram job (ETA Wed), tara -> privacy retention rules for obsv.cost.v1 (ETA Tue), john -> reconciliation runbook + threshold (ETA Fri). I'll draft a short RFC w/ diagrams.

diego (runtime): One more thought: for clients that use Dedicated/private deployments we should support opt-out of telemetry header. Add flag in deployment config.

nina (observability): Noted. We'll only reconcile hosted/managed by default. For private, require customer opt-in in config.

clare (eng-platform): Sounds good. We'll hold on backfill decision until we see canary delta. Thanks all — closing thread, will link RFC when ready. :white_check_mark:
